mentl/36bd28e:
The previous entry claimed decl-side handler state-init expressions are
never inferred, reasoning from register_handler performing only the
op-shadow check. That is false. The judging lives elsewhere in the same
file — infer_handler_state_inits — whose neighbouring comment states the
contract outright: config params bound first, so a state init
referencing one reads the live config. It even records the bug that
motivated it.

Two seconds of probe refute the claim. handler h(start) with n =
nosuchname + 1 reports E_MissingVariable at 5:30-5:40 and mentl run
refuses at exit 1. Inits are judged and unbound names in them refuse.

How the error was made, recorded because it is the same one twice in a
day: I read one site, found it insufficient, and generalised to "never"
without grepping for a second reader. Before writing "never" about a
compiler, run the program that would prove it.

What is actually true: infer resolves a config ref in a state init
correctly, so a clean check is the right answer rather than a missed
diagnostic. Lower is the gap. lower_state_init matches only a top-level
VarRef against config names and turns it into LUpval(0, slot);
everything else goes through lower_expr, where the config name is not in
the lowering scope, resolves RGlobal, misses env_kind_of, and becomes
the MissingName floor. The site's comment has said so all along.

The defect that survives is narrower and still real: a construct the
lowering cannot lower produces a runtime floor rather than a refusal, so
the program checks clean and traps.

And the fix is smaller than either story suggested. The lowering scope
already carries an RUpval verdict, so the config ref needs no capture
frame, only a way to declare one — ls_bind_upval beside ls_bind_local, a
scope pushed in lower_state_field_inits binding each config name to its
slot. Then lower_state_init's special case dissolves into the general
resolver: the fix deletes a special case instead of adding one.

perennials/3621e98:
The sources record a continent; she records a yard. USDA's Late Spring
is an average across every zone it covers; third week of May, by the
fence, is true. A note is one free-text entry per plant, dated, stored
beside the kept list, and the lanes never mix: source values are never
edited, her words are never attributed to a source, and the colophon's
source table gains its fourth row — You. Written on this phone, kept on
this phone, sent nowhere, which the editor also says at the moment of
writing.

On the plant page the note sits where an annotation sits on a herbarium
sheet: above the printed record, sepia rule, her words in the display
face. On the Kept page it is the line under the card. A note is not a
keep — avoid, spreads like hell, is a decision against a plant and must
not put it in the bloom year — so noted-but-not-kept plants get their
own shelf, and no one-tap delete: un-keeping discards a bookmark,
deleting a note destroys her words, so that takes the editor.

Save a copy writes the whole notebook to plain text, through the share
sheet where there is one. localStorage is one factory reset from gone;
paper is the only format guaranteed to outlive the app.

stoop/36f8f40:
The press drew the imposed sheet as its editing surface, so four of the
eight panels were upside down while somebody was typing into them, and
the paste-up grew a pile of machinery to drag things across a panel
rotated half a turn. That was the printer's view of the zine, faithfully
reproduced for the one person who should never have to see it. Nobody
making a zine thinks in printer slots.

The press now shows pages: the cover on its own, facing spreads, the back
cover, right way up, in reading order, each the size it will print at so
the fit meter still measures real paper, the whole run zoomed to the
column. The imposition is a property of paper and is applied on the way
there. The PDF writer already imposed from the model; browser printing
now goes through the same static sheet the shelf reprints and the
exported issue use, rendered into the print zone and emptied when the
dialog closes, and printing from the keyboard gets the sheet too. The
numbered test sheet is printed rather than toggled over the pages,
because it exists to verify a fold and there is no fold on screen.

The upside-down drag case is gone with the surface that needed it, and
the suites that asserted it now assert the opposite: no page on the press
is ever upside down, dragging right goes right on every page, the pages
read one to eight on screen, and what the browser is handed to print
imposes as preset A with nothing else visible.
